**What you’re asking:** You want the app to remember every customer’s card so that on a future checkout they can just pick the card from a list, instead of typing everything again. **Why this is a Red‑level feature** * It stores payment‑card details (PCI data). * It involves money and external payment services (Stripe). * It requires strict security (key handling, PCI compliance, user data limits). Because of that, we’ll keep the plan small, save‑point every step, and double‑check that your secrets stay on the server. --- ## One‑screen plan (Version 1) | ✔ | Item | |---|------| | **What we’re building** | “Save customers' cards so future checkouts can use a drop‑down list of their own cards.” | | **Who uses it** | All logged‑in users of the app (anyone who can checkout). | | **Risk level** | **Red** – because of money and sensitive card data. | | **Day‑one features** | 1. User can add a card to their account. 2. Card appears in a “Saved cards” list when checking out. 3. 4. Update the checkout page to fetch the user’s saved card IDs, display a drop‑down, and use the selected card when creating a payment.
5. Add database RLS rules so only the owner can read/write the card IDs. | | **Safety** | Secrets kept in `.env` (server only). RLS rules on the card table.
